title: Office Cleaning Minimum Charge per Visit: Why $90 to $135 Floors Apply
seoTitle: Office Cleaning Minimum Charge per Visit: $90–$135 Trip Floors
metaDescription: Office cleaning minimum charge per visit averages $90–$135 in the US to cover mobilization and 2-hour labor floors. Run our calculator or compare bids.
excerpt: Small suites under 750 sq ft rarely pay pure square-footage math because commercial janitorial contractors enforce a $90 to $135 minimum charge per visit. Learn the dispatch math behind trip floors, when your suite crosses above the minimum, and five ways to capture full value from every billed visit.
quickAnswer: Most US commercial cleaning contractors enforce an office cleaning minimum charge per visit of $90 to $135 (scaling from $77–$115 in 0.85x lower-cost metros up to $122–$182 in 1.35x Tier-1 cities). This floor covers vehicle dispatch, building security check-in, equipment unloading, and a two-hour minimum labor allocation—meaning offices under ~650–750 sq ft typically pay the flat minimum regardless of raw square-footage math.

blocks.text: Managers of compact 400 to 650 sq ft medical suites, insurance agencies, and satellite law offices are often surprised when a **$0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft** quote turns into a **$110 or $135 per-visit invoice**. On paper, 500 sq ft multiplied by $0.16/sq ft equals just $80—yet almost no insured commercial cleaning company will dispatch an evening technician for $80.

The discrepancy comes from the **minimum charge per visit** (`$90 to $135` national baseline), a universal trip floor built into legitimate commercial contracts. Understanding exactly where the minimum overrides square-footage math helps small-office buyers budget accurately alongside our [small office cleaning monthly budget guide](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/small-office-cleaning-monthly-budget-guide/) and extract maximum scope from every paid stop.
Why Commercial Cleaners Enforce a $90 to $135 Minimum Trip Fee

Unlike a solo residential cleaner working cash-in-hand, a W-2 commercial janitorial vendor absorbs substantial fixed mobilization costs before a vacuum ever turns on. Even if a 500 sq ft suite takes only 35 minutes of active wiping and vacuuming, the contractor incurs unbillable overhead at every stop.

items: **Vehicle Drive Time & Fuel:** Evening route crews typically spend 15 to 25 minutes driving and parking between commercial office parks or downtown garages.
**Security Check-In & Key Control:** Sign-in at lobby security desks, alarm disarming, supply-closet unlocking, and final lock-up easily consume 15 to 20 paid minutes per visit.

**Two-Hour Labor Floor Laws & Retention:** Cleaners will not commute for a 45-minute shift; paying technicians a 2-hour minimum block at $35–$65/hr billed rates sets an economic floor near **$90 to $135**.

**Insurance, Bonding & OSHA Paperwork:** Active $1M/$2M General Liability coverage, W-2 Workers' Compensation, fidelity bonding, and HazCom SDS kits carry fixed per-account overhead regardless of suite size.

blocks.text: Exact Crossover Math: When Small Offices Outgrow the Minimum Floor

Under our [national office cleaning cost benchmarks](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/), suites under 2,500 sq ft start at **$0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft** plus **$15 to $30 per private restroom**. Because weekly frequency multipliers also adjust raw pricing (`1.08x` for 1x/week vs `0.95x` for 3x/week and `0.90x` for 5x/week), a **600 to 750 sq ft suite with one private restroom** is the exact inflection point where calculated square-footage pricing rises above the **$90–$135** trip floor.

blocks.title: Notice How 400 Sq Ft and 500 Sq Ft Pay Identical 3x/Week Bills
blocks.text: Both a 400 sq ft suite (no restroom) and a 500 sq ft suite (1 restroom) hit the full $90–$135 minimum on a 3x/week schedule—costing $1,170 to $1,755 per month. If you are budgeting a micro-suite, never use raw sq-ft multipliers without checking the minimum floor first.
How Regional Labor Markets Shift Minimum Visit Charges

Just like hourly and square-footage rates, minimum trip charges scale with local wages, parking fees, and Workers' Compensation costs. In congested downtown cores where technicians pay $20 to $35 for evening garage parking or wait 15 minutes at security turnstiles, minimum visit fees climb sharply.

blocks.text: 5 Ways to Maximize Value Inside a Minimum-Charge Visit

Because a minimum fee buys roughly **1.25 to 2.00 hours of technician availability**, you can often absorb detail tasks that larger suites pay extra for—without pushing your invoice above the trip floor. Before renegotiating, model different visit frequencies in our [Office Cleaning Cost Calculator](/office-cleaning-cost-calculator/) and review [flat-rate vs. hourly office cleaning pricing](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/flat-rate-vs-hourly-office-cleaning-pricing/).

items.name: Bundle Interior Glass and Breakroom Wipe-Downs Into the Minimum
items.text: In a 500 sq ft suite, ask your vendor to include conference partition glass, microwave interiors, and entry sidelights inside the $90–$135 base visit rather than as separate add-ons.

items.name: Shift From 3x/Week to 1x/Week + Daytime Staff Touchups
items.text: Dropping from 3x/week ($1,170–$1,755/mo) to 1x/week ($390–$598/mo) cuts annual spend by over $9,000 while keeping full deep weekly sanitization intact.

items.name: Co-Bid With Adjacent Suites on Your Floor
items.text: If two neighboring 500 sq ft tenants hire the same contractor on the same evening, the vendor eliminates a second vehicle trip and can often waive or split the individual trip floor.

items.name: Avoid Parking Surprises in Downtown Towers
items.text: Validate or designate a loading-zone pass for evening techs so a $25 parking fee isn't permanently baked into your minimum visit rate.

items.name: Verify Exact 4.333 Weeks/Month Retainer Math
items.text: Confirm your monthly minimum-visit retainer averages 4.33 visits/month (1x/wk) or 13.00 visits/month (3x/wk) with no surprise fifth-week billing.

blocks.title: Equip Receptionists for Quick Between-Visit Touchups
blocks.text: When stretching a 500–750 sq ft suite to weekly ($390–$831/mo) or biweekly professional service, keeping three compact daytime tools in a coat closet lets staff clear crumbs or entryway litter in 90 seconds without triggering an extra vendor visit.
Compact Daytime Touchup Gear That Cuts Vendor Frequency

For suites dropping from 3x/week to 1x/week vendor visits, lightweight daytime spot tools keep client lobbies presentable between stops. Along exterior sidewalks and parking aprons, the **Unger Nifty Nabber 36-Inch Commercial Trash Picker Grabber** uses steel claws with rubber tips and a 10-lb lift capacity so staff clear entry litter safely without bending. Inside reception lobbies, the **Rubbermaid Commercial Lobby Pro Upright Dust Pan & Broom** pairs quiet wheels and an automatic self-opening lid with a long handle for discreet daytime crumb sweeps. For executive carpet runners or conference room chairs, the **Dyson V15 Detect Pro / Commercial Spot Cordless Stick** weighs 6.8 lb with whole-machine HEPA sealing, particle detection, and up to 60 minutes of runtime for silent, cord-free spot touchups before client meetings.

faqs.q: At what square footage does an office cleaning minimum charge stop applying?
faqs.a: In average 1.00x US markets, an office with one private restroom typically crosses above the $90–$135 minimum visit fee around 650 to 750 cleanable sq ft. Below 600 sq ft (or up to ~750 sq ft without private restrooms), raw square-footage math falls below $90 and triggers the flat minimum.

faqs.q: Can I negotiate a lower minimum visit charge on a 500 sq ft office?
faqs.a: Occasionally, yes—if your contractor already cleans another tenant in the exact same building or office park on the same night, eliminating separate drive time and parking fees. Otherwise, legitimate W-2 insured cleaners rarely drop below $85–$100/visit without sacrificing background checks or liability insurance.

faqs.q: Does a minimum charge include paper towels, toilet paper, and trash liners?
faqs.a: No. Minimum visit fees cover technician mobilization, labor, vacuuming, mopping, and vendor cleaning chemicals. Paper consumables and trash liners are either supplied by your office or billed separately ($0.012 to $0.025/sq ft/visit, or flat case markups).

faqs.q: Are small offices still required to verify a janitorial vendor's COI?
faqs.a: Yes—even for a 400 sq ft suite on a minimum-fee visit. Most commercial landlords require every vendor holding building keys or access fobs to provide an active Certificate of Insurance ($1M/$2M General Liability naming tenant and landlord as Additional Insured), W-2 Workers' Compensation, and fidelity bonding.

faqs.q: What OSHA compliance rules apply to small-suite minimum-fee cleanings?
faqs.a: Under OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200), contractors bringing chemical bottles onto your premises must label secondary containers and supply accessible Safety Data Sheets (SDS). If they service private restrooms, OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) PPE training still applies.
